key_claims.claim: Uterine artery pulsatility index at 35-36 weeks correlates with angiogenic imbalance, altered maternal hemodynamics, and increased vascular stiffness in women who develop preeclampsia
Persistent fetal sinus bradycardia is associated with a substantial risk of serious postnatal cardiac diagnoses including structural defects, conduction abnormalities, and cardiomyopathies
Fetal autopsy counseling and completion rates after stillbirth are low and associated with identifiable patient and clinician factors that vary across institutions
Cervical insufficiency should be redefined operationally around evidence-based cerclage indications rather than traditional clinical diagnosis
Machine learning models using administrative health records can predict preterm birth at 26 weeks with modest but scalable population-level performance
